a.summary: COMPILE ERROR. The merge base had `import static software.sava.core.accounts.meta.AccountMeta.*;`. v1_tx narrowed it to explicit `createRead` / `createWrite` imports; main left it as the wildcard, so git silently took v1_tx's narrowed block. But main's `invokedProgramAccount(...)` helper (2c70f78) survived the auto-merge at lines 299-305 and calls `createInvoked(account.publicKey())`, which no longer resolves. v1_tx's feature work lost the symbol main's fix depends on.

b.summary: COMPILE ERROR (confirmed by javac). The merge base had `import static software.sava.core.accounts.meta.AccountMeta.*;`. v1_tx narrowed it to explicit `createRead` / `createWrite` imports; main kept the wildcard, so git silently took v1_tx's narrowed block. But main's `invokedProgramAccount(...)` helper (2c70f78) survived the auto-merge at lines 299-305 and calls `createInvoked(account.publicKey())` at line 304, which no longer resolves. Static imports are per-file, so BaseTransactionSkeleton's own wildcard does not help. v1_tx's feature work lost the symbol main's fix depends on.

instructions.question: How does the defect described by `b` relate to the defect described by `a`?
instructions.focus: Compare the defects, not the wording. Two findings about the same code can still be different defects.

criteria: Different defects: fixing the defect `a` describes would leave the defect `b` describes unfixed, even when both sit in the same code.
The same underlying defect, but `b` narrows it, re-scopes which instances or inputs it covers, or reports it at a different place. Not a different defect in adjacent code.
The same defect restated in different words: fixing one fixes the other.

claims_new_evidence.instructions: Does `b` cite evidence that `a` does not?

criteria.true: `b` names a file, test, command, observation, or reproduction that `a` does not mention.
criteria.false: `b` cites nothing beyond what `a` already cites, or cites nothing at all.
